entries.name: IDS_INTERCEPTMSG
entries.text: Is it OK to scramble against this raid?

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_1_DESC
entries.text:
In this training exercise you will practice engine start-up and take-off.
(NOTE: If the 'Engine Management' option in SIM Flight Prefs is set to 'Auto' then your engine will already be running as you start the mission)

Your aircraft is parked at the take-off point and the area is clear of all other traffic.

The station commander is looking for a quick and clean take-off - don't bounce.

He will comment on your performance when you are safely airborne.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_2_DESC
entries.text:
This practice session will test your ability to land your fighter safely.

Your aircraft is on final approach so all you need worry about is flaps, gear, height and speed.

The station commander will give an assessment of your landing when you are down so try to do so smoothly without bouncing. Good luck.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_3_DESC
entries.text:
In this landing exercise you will make a circuit around the airfield in order to position yourself for a final approach.

Again, the station commander will be assessing your performance.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_4_DESC
entries.text:
The squadron is lined up for a formation take-off

(NOTE: If the 'Engine Management' option in SIM Flight Prefs is set to 'Auto' then your engine will already be running as you start the mission)

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_5_DESC
entries.text:
You are approaching your airfield with the rest of your squadron.

The whole squadron is going to put down.
Listen for orders and be aware of the proximity of your wingmen.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_6_DESC
entries.text:
You are within sight of your airfield but your engine is failing.

You must attempt an emergency glide landing.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_7_DESC
entries.text:
Your aircraft has sustained some battle damage.

You must nurse it back to your field and make an emergency landing.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_8_DESC
entries.text:
Your Squadron Leader has taken you up to test your flying skill.

He will make a number of evasive manoeuvres to throw you off his tail.

Get into an ideal firing position and stay close - but be careful not to clip him!

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_9_DESC
entries.text:
The squadron is practising formation flying.

The leader will initiate a sequence of course changes.

He expects everyone to maintain his position in the formation.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_10_DESC
entries.text:
You are flying alone within sight of your home field.

You are free to fly through the surrounding area to familiarise yourself with the region.

Look for landmarks that will help you to locate your field in future.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_11_DESC
entries.text:
You are lined up behind a totally oblivious enemy fighter.

All you have to do is keep him in your sights and pull the trigger.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_12_DESC
entries.text:
Most engagements break down into individual combats; Man against Man, Machine against Machine.

Only one of you can emerge from this confrontation victorious.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_13_DESC
entries.text:
A British squadron has been vectored to engage an enemy fighter sweep.

The RAF force was slow to scramble so there is a possibility that they will not be in an advantageous position.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_14_DESC
entries.text: RAF controllers have carefully vectored a Squadron to the rear of a force of Luftwaffe fighters, the perfect position to deliver an attack.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_15_DESC
entries.text:
A Luftwaffe fighter sweep has discovered an RAF patrol.

The German fighters have worked their way behind and are now ready to deliver a punishing attack.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_TO_TRAINING
entries.text: You need to practise getting off the ground as quickly as possible.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_WELLDONE_TO
entries.text: Well done. A nice clean take-off

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_MINCEMEAT
entries.text: If this was a real scramble, you would be mincemeat by now.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BADLAND0
entries.text: At least you're down in one piece.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BADLAND1
entries.text: Well, that was a close run thing.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BADLAND2
entries.text: That gave you a good shaking. I hope it did some good!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_DAMAGEONLANDING0
entries.text: Well, you just about got away with it.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LANDEDDAMAGEDAC1
entries.text: You were lucky to get that down.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LANDEDBADLYDAMAGEDAC0
entries.text: You did well to get back in one piece.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ACPRODUCTIONFULFILLED1
entries.text: has received its quota of fighters.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ALLPROD
entries.text: will receive all production until further notice.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_INCONTACT1
entries.text: is in contact with the enemy.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RESTNORTH0
entries.text: They are going north for a rest.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RESTNORTH1
entries.text: They are going north for a well earned breather.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RESTNORTH2
entries.text: They are going north for some peace and quiet.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_MORESQUADRON
entries.text: Better bring more squadrons to stand by.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ALLUP0
entries.text: All squadrons are in the air.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_TRADEFORYOU
entries.text: I have some trade for you

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_HAVEFIX
entries.text: I have a fix on you

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_INCONTACTLW1
entries.text: is in contact with the enemy.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_REPORTSSUCCESS1
entries.text: has carried out a successful operation.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAIDFAIL0
entries.text: reports failure. It met fierce resistance.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAIDFAIL1
entries.text: intercepted and prevented from carrying out a successful mission.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAIDFAIL3
entries.text: did not reach its intended target.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_REMIND0
entries.text: The Luftflotte are on standby, awaiting your orders.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_REMIND1
entries.text: As you have cancelled all directives, we await your direct orders.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_MONUMENTSURVIVES0
entries.text: survived the attentions of the Luftwaffe.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RECORDKILLS
entries.text: In today's action, the brave pilots of the RAF accounted for a record number of enemy raiders. Even though fighting under extreme conditions, our pilots are increasing the pressure on the Luftwaffe.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PHASE2BEGINS
entries.text: In what seems a definite change in strategy, the Luftwaffe are now targeting our Radio Direction Finding Network.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PHASE3BEGINS
entries.text: The Luftwaffe have now moved onto attacking our fighter bases. Ground crews are confident they can endure whatever the Luftwaffe visit upon them.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PHASE4BEGINS
entries.text: It seems that our Fighter bases have survived the Luftwaffe assault. Attacks are now centring on London. This gives our fighter stations desperately needed time to regroup.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BIGESCORT
entries.text: Luftwaffe bomber formations are now being escorted by increased numbers of fighters: at least 2 fighters for every bomber. This tactic limits the number of bombers the Germans can have in the air at any one time.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ACFACTORYOUT
entries.text: Our aircraft factories have taken a beating recently.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_DISPERSALBAD
entries.text: The facility's entire production will be lost because the dispersed sites are not ready.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RECORDKILLS1
entries.text: In yesterday's action, the gallant pilots of the Luftwaffe accounted for a record number of enemy aircraft.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RECORDKILLS2
entries.text: Fighter Command is being decimated. This is a day to celebrate.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RECORDKILLS3
entries.text: They can't have many more fighters available.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RECORDLOSSES1
entries.text: That is our worst day of the campaign so far.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BIGWINGUSED
entries.text: The RAF are using a new tactic of massed formations. Close groups of 3 or more enemy squadrons are being encountered by our bombers.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_SEALION
entries.text: Preparations for Operation Sealion are continuing apace. The invasion is scheduled to begin in 2 weeks. Every barge and transport of the required size has been moved to the coastal harbours.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LUFWIN1
entries.text: The Luftwaffe's objectives have been achieved. The RAF is no more. Operation Sealion will be launched tomorrow. The British fleet will try to intervene but will be destroyed from the air. Our troops will storm the English beaches. The South will be isolated. London will be encircled. Victory will be ours...

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LUFWIN2
entries.text: The RAF has been totally wiped out. The British government must surely see the futility of its position and accept our conditions. If not, Operation Sealion will be launched early to force the issue.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LUFWIN3
entries.text: This is truly our darkest hour. The RAF is a broken and spent force. The Luftwaffe rules the skies above England. When the invasion comes, and we must assume it will be soon, we will be hard pressed to stop them. Still, we will fight on...

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LUFWIN4
entries.text: RAF totally wiped out. Invasion imminent

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFDECIMATED
entries.text: Intelligence reports that RAF are suffering terrible losses. They are now down to their last 50 Spitfires!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFWIN
entries.text: We have prevailed in our darkest hour. Winter is approaching and conditions in the Channel are deteriorating. The threat of invasion is diminishing. German forces are leaving the coastal areas.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFHEADON
entries.text: Our pilots claim that the most effective form of attack against the massed enemy bomber formations is the head-on pass. Luftwaffe bombers project less forward firepower and the crew is gathered together in the vulnerable front cockpit.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFPAC0
entries.text: : PAC trials encouraging. PAC (Parachute and Cable) defences were responsible for bringing down at least one low-flying raider at the airfield. A rocket fires a cable upwards which is then held aloft by a deployed parachute. PACs are fired in unison for maximum effect.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RDFHOLES
entries.text: Although the RDF network has been breached, we are covering up by using our mobile units.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_WINSTON
entries.text: Winston Churchill has visited some of the civilian areas hit by Luftwaffe bombs. The fighting spirit of those people whose homes lay in ruins impressed him. People cheered as the Prime Minister picked his way through the debris to talk to the families.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ROYAL
entries.text: The King and Queen visited areas that have recently sustained bomb damage. They chatted to members of the public who had been affected.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_CANNON
entries.text: We have assessed the effects of cannon fire on the airframes of British aircraft. We believe that the fighters often survive hits because low muzzle velocity causes the shells to explode before penetrating the airframe.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFMSC1
entries.text: A note has been issued to homeguard units to curb accidental shootings. Some over-excited individuals, believing themselves witness to a paratroop drop, have taken potshots at lone parachutists.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFMSC2
entries.text: Pilots report that tail-end Charlie is regarded as the most dangerous position to fly in.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFMSC3
entries.text: Some pilots feel the need to add an extra few thousand feet to the altitude stated by the controller. They fear that they me be caught beneath enemy fighters. This sometimes leads to missed interceptions.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFMSC4
entries.text: We would like to remind all pilots that using station petrol bowsers to fill up the tanks of their private vehicles is against regulations.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFRADIONET0
entries.text: We believe that our raids against the British Radio Net have so far been ineffective.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFRADIONET1
entries.text: Radio signals from sites that have been attacked are still detectable.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFRADIONET2
entries.text: Presumably, the vulnerable parts of the system are well protected underground.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LUFPAC0
entries.text: : New defence found. Our pilots report a new weapon active at this airfield that may be responsible for some of our losses in low-level raids. Witnesses say that rockets have been fired vertically, in unison, around the perimeter of the field. We have no more information.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LUFMSC1
entries.text: The best way to attack docks is by flying through the harbour entrance where balloons cannot be deployed easily.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LUFMSC2
entries.text: British fighters suffer from the inferior carburettor feed of their engines. When performing negative-g manoeuvres, British engines are prone to stuttering as fuel flow is momentarily cut off. Our superior direct fuel injection engines do not suffer from this fault.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LUFMSC3
entries.text: Command would like to remind those pilots staying in the Region's Chateaus that the rarer vintage wines in the cellars are prohibited. They must be put aside for collection by a staff officer.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_REVIEWKILL
entries.text: claimed today. Our forces had limited success today.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_REVIEWKILL2
entries.text: claimed today. Our forces have reported numerous successes today. Generally a good day all around.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_REVIEWLOSS
entries.text: losses today. Our forces have suffered at the hands of the enemy today.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_REVIEWLOSS2
entries.text: losses today. Today's losses are devastating. Our forces are demoralized.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RSTOPCOVER
entries.text: Attack Bombers, others on Top Cover

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_DESTROYED1
entries.text: now out of action. If this goes on we'll be blind soon.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_GROUNDRANGE
entries.text: The raid is entering their ground range.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LOSTCONTACT0
entries.text: We've lost contact with them, Sir.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LOSTCONTACT1
entries.text: The line to Sector Ops is dead, Sir.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_MOBILEFILLGAP
entries.text: Mobile units are filling the radar gap.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LITTLEDAMAGE2
entries.text: was slightly damaged in that raid.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BIGDAMAGE0
entries.text: took a pounding. We are lucky it is still operational.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BIGDAMAGE1
entries.text: is a mess. It will be some time before they clear it up.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ALLSUNK
entries.text: All ships in the convoy have now been sunk.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAIDSPLITS1
entries.text: update. ROC reports seeing groups splitting from the main force.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAIDSPLITS2
entries.text: . Reports that it has split up are coming in.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ONCOURSE
entries.text: is now on a direct course.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FIGHTERSSUCCESS
entries.text: Our fighters have succesfully diverted them.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_DUMPBOMBS
entries.text: There are reports of bombs falling on the countryside.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PRODHAMPERED1
entries.text: Fighter production has been badly hit.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_VECTORINTGRND
entries.text: Have you got a vector to my target?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OUTNUMBERED0
entries.text: Bloody Hell, Where are they all coming from?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OUTNUMBERED1
entries.text: The sky's full of enemy fighters

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OUTNUMBERED2
entries.text: For Pete's sake. There are just too many of them.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PLAYERDAMAGE1LOW2
entries.text: He got me, he got me!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PLAYERDAMAGE2LOW3
entries.text: I'm hit, get him off me!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PLAYERDAMAGE2MED3
entries.text: I can't shake him off me!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_WATCHFORESCORT2
entries.text: Watch out for the fighter escort.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RAFLOWFUEL
entries.text: I'm running short of gravy here.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ORBITFORFIX
entries.text: I am orbiting position and transmitting for fix

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_SPLITUP
entries.text: We have all been split up

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_REARMFL
entries.text: Aircraft are landing to re-arm and re-fuel

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FORMATIONFIRING
entries.text: When I say Bingo, everybody Fire!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ITSSUICIDE
entries.text: It's a suicide run but my God, they scatter.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LACE
entries.text: I say old boy, what's that you're flying- a piece of lace?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_HOLES
entries.text: You're crates collected a few holes. Try sticking your arms out and flap.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_TROUBLE
entries.text: I say you're in real trouble and no mistake.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_VECTORPATROL
entries.text: Do you have a vector to my patrol area?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_VECTORINT
entries.text: Do you have a vector to my intercept?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OTHERTRADE
entries.text: Do you have any other trade for me?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_SKYCLEAR
entries.text: The sky seems clear of bandits today.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_THANKSANDGO
entries.text: Thanks for the support, you can leave us now.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_STARTINGTRGTRUN0
entries.text: Arm your bomb and follow me in.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_STARTINGTRGTRUN1
entries.text: Arm your bombs and follow me in.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_VECTORESCORT
entries.text: Does anybody have a vector to my bombers?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OPENWIDE
entries.text: Open it up- good and wide!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_EYES_PEELED2
entries.text: Everyone keep your eyes peeled for the escort.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_EYES_PEELED3
entries.text: The lot of you keep your eyes peeled.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_GETBACK
entries.text: what are you doing out there? Get back.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PROPCHEW
entries.text: Don't chew off my tail with your ruddy prop!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_SUPPOSEDFOLLOW
entries.text: You're supposed to be following me.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_WHEREHELLGOING
entries.text: where the hell are you going?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_CLOSEUP2
entries.text: I don't want to see daylight.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_CLOSEUP4
entries.text: For Pete's sake, close it up!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_CLOSEUP5
entries.text: Much closer. I can hardly see you.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_CLOSEUP6
entries.text: You must keep up with me.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_GLIDE
entries.text: I'm going to try to glide home

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ONESWEEP
entries.text: We'll make one more sweep and then go home.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LOOKDOWN
entries.text: Look down there, that aircraft is in trouble.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BANDITSOUTTHERE
entries.text: I've got some bandits out there

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ASSISTCONFIRM0
entries.text: Let's go and help them out.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_GETINFIRST
entries.text: Get in first. Let's jimmy the straggler.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LETGO1
entries.text: We have other problems right now.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OUTNUMBEREDREPLY0
entries.text: Keep them busy. I'll join you.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OTHERDAMAGE1HI1
entries.text: I've got a bead on him now.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OTHERDAMAGE2HI1
entries.text: Come on, just a few more should do it...

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OTHERDAMAGE2HI3
entries.text: A few more seconds should do it...

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_SMELLSMOKEPLUS
entries.text: I can smell smoke, I must have engine damage

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_GOTHIMLEAKING0
entries.text: I hit him, he's streaming glycol.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_GOTHIMLEAKING1
entries.text: I hit him, he's losing glycol.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_AMICLEARTOLAND
entries.text: Tower, am I clear to land?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_AMICLEARTOPANCAKE
entries.text: Tower, am I clear to pancake?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ALTWINDREQUEST
entries.text: Tower, what's the wind at altitude?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_GIMMEAVECTOR
entries.text: Tower, can you give me a vector, over?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_GRPGOHOME1
entries.text: Close it up and let's go home.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_DONEASMUCH
entries.text: We have done as much as we can.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_WAKEHOME
entries.text: Let's wake them up at home

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ITSDIVEANDZOOM
entries.text: It's a Dive and Zoom attack.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_IGNOREFORNOW2
entries.text: We can leave them for now.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_TURNINSIDE
entries.text: He's getting a bead on me...can't beat him in the turn!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_CLOSEANDFIRING1
entries.text: I've a bandit close in and he's firing!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ASKFORHELP0
entries.text: I'm under attack, I need help!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LOOKBLIGHTER
entries.text: Watch the blighter-smack behind you, man, behind you!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BREAKHELL
entries.text: Break and give them hell, NOW!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BOASTKILL0
entries.text: Did you see me get him? I got him!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BOASTKILL1
entries.text: I got one! I got one! Do you see him?

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_BOASTKILL3
entries.text: I bagged one! He blew up!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_OTHERKILLED1
entries.text: I got him, I got him chaps.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_ENEMYSMOKING3
entries.text: That's a claim. Look at the smoke!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FIREINENGINE
entries.text: There's a fire in your engine!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_NEVERMAKEIT
entries.text: You'll never make it. Get out before it blows up!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_COMINGINBEHIND
entries.text: we have some bandits coming in behind us!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_COMINGINABEAM
entries.text: we have some bandits coming in from my

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_COMINGINAHEAD
entries.text: we have some bandits coming at us!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FF_NOTBAD0
entries.text: Not bad, but there's still room for improvement.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FF_NOTBAD1
entries.text: You are getting the hang of it but you still need practice.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FF_NOTGOOD0
entries.text: I've seen enough. You're proving less than useless.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FF_NOTGOOD1
entries.text: You'll have to go up again tomorrow. You are nowhere near ready.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FF_GOOD0
entries.text: Excellent. I'd gladly have you on my wing in combat.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FF_GOOD1
entries.text: Good Show. You are certainly ready for the real thing.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_FF_GOOD2
entries.text: Well done! You've passed the test!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_LEFTBEHIND0
entries.text: No, No. We'll have to try that again. I was losing you.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_TOOFAST0
entries.text: I can't keep up with you.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_TOOFAST1
entries.text: Slow down, I can't keep up.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PLAYERDAMAGECOWARD0
entries.text: Taken some hits, I'm leaving the party.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_PLAYERDAMAGE2CONV0RR0
entries.text: Right. I'm going to have to bale out!

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_SMOKINGBADLY1
entries.text: There's black smoke pouring out of your engine

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_CHECKFUEL
entries.text: Re-check your fuel, you should have plenty.

entries.name: IDS_PHRASE_RATSINBARREL
entries.text: This is better than shooting rats in a barrel!

entries.name: IDS_L_CONVOYDESC
entries.text:
During this phase the Luftwaffe attacked British shipping in the channel. Their aim was to entice the RAF over the channel where neither side had the territorial advantage.
Fighter Command were ordered to defend the Merchant Navy but were reluctant to weaken their force prior to the main battle of the Summer.

entries.name: IDS_EAGLEATTACK
entries.text:
During this phase the Luftwaffe attacked British radar sites and RAF airfields. Their aim was to eliminate the RAF as a fighting force prior to the invasion planned for September.
Fighter Commander received little warning of the attacks and did not have the time to marshal their resources. Small groups of Spitfires and Hurricanes were sent out to respond to the might of the Luftwaffe.

entries.name: IDS_CRITICALPERIOD
entries.text:
During this phase the Luftwaffe concentrated on the RAF's large inland airfields and the British aircraft manufacturing industry.
As with

entries.name: IDS_BLITZ
entries.text:
During this phase the Luftwaffe attacked London. This was planned to be the final phase before the invasion.
The RAF was forced to defend its capital city. However the Luftwaffe fighters were on the limit of their endurance and the RAF had plenty of time to respond. As a result the RAF were able to respond with large formations of fighters. This was the time for the Big Wing.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_17_DESC
entries.text:
Luftwaffe dive-bombers are approaching their target.

The RAF have a scrambled a response but the climbing fighters will present an easy target for the German fighter escort.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_18_DESC
entries.text:
A convoy in the Channel has attracted a swarm of Dive-Bombers.

An RAF patrol has been diverted to intercept.

German fighters are in the area.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_19_DESC
entries.text:
German aircraft are approaching a coastal target at low level to evade detection by radar.

They hope to deliver a sudden attack and escape before a response is raised.

Unfortunately, a British patrol is in the area.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_20_DESC
entries.text:
A lone RAF fighter has been scrambled to deal with a single raider.

The intruder is a fully laden bomber hoping to make a snap raid.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_21_DESC
entries.text:
2 RAF fighter squadrons in close formation have been vectored AHEAD of an enemy bomber force.

2 fighter squadrons are providing close escort for the raiders.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_22_DESC
entries.text:
2 RAF fighter squadrons in close formation have been vectored to the REAR of an enemy bomber force.

2 fighter squadrons are providing close escort for the raiders.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_23_DESC
entries.text:
2 RAF squadrons have been directed to the reported position of an enemy raid.

The RAF squadrons have been unable to form up together and are unsure where the bombers are.

Also, 2 Luftwaffe fighter squadrons are sweeping through the area.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_26_DESC
entries.text:
Until this day, the Defiant had enjoyed some success in the fighter role.

Luftwaffe pilots mistaking the Defiant for one of its counterparts, the Hurricane, would make rear attacks in full view of the Defiant's 4 gun turret.

The German's quickly learned to exploit the Defiant's lack of forward firepower by making low frontal attacks.

On this day a total massacre was only avoided due to the intervention of a Hurricane squadron.

It was enough to bring about the withdrawal of the Defiant from daylight operations.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_28_DESC
entries.text:
Eagle Day saw the start of a new campaign directed inland against fighter command.
Bad weather in the morning resulted in abortive raids.

In the afternoon, as conditions cleared, numerous raids were inbound along a 40 mile stretch of the Dorset coast.

40 Ju88s and an escort sweep of 30 Me 110s on the west flank tried to hit Portland but were hindered by 3 RAF Squadrons.

3 Ju88 Gruppen opposed by 24 fighters pushed through to Southampton and caused heavy damage.

30 Ju87 heading to Middle Wallop were smashed by the station's Spitfire Squadron.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_29_DESC
entries.text:
This day saw a final defeat for the Luftwaffe forces at the moment they expected the British defence to fold.

2 massive raids launched against London were met in force by rested and re-deployed Squadrons.

The bombers were slowly stripped of their escort as they neared their target.

There they were hit head-on by 4 Hurricane Squadrons as the Duxford Wing wheeled in across the flank.

As the shattered formations of Bombers retreated in disarray there was no doubt that the RAF were stronger than ever.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_30_DESC
entries.text:
2 gruppen of bombers are approaching Southampton. Each gruppe consists of 3 staffel of bombers closely escorted by 3 staffel of fighters.
You have the opportunity to fly in any aircraft from the lead staffel of either wave.

The RAF response consists of 2 squadrons of fighters.
You can fly any of these aircraft.

You can alter the number of flights that appear in each staffel or squadron.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_31_DESC
entries.text:
A spate of raids in the late evening were launched against factories in the South London suburbs.

26 He 111s with an escort of 60 Bf 109s and 20 Bf 110s were briefed to attack Farnborough.

Their westerly course across South London gave fighter stations in the area time to mount an aggressive response.

8 paired squadrons attacked simultaneously, discouraging the escort already low on fuel.

1 Staffel of He 111s broke away and sought an escape route to the south.

As it neared Biggin Hill, this Staffel came across another raid consisting of 40 Ju88s under heavy attack from 2 Hurricane squadrons.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_32_DESC
entries.text:
Black Thursday saw some of the hardest fighting of the whole Battle.

Raid signals were so massive that Sector controllers had trouble directing fighters to specific raids.

This slow reaction resulted in the shock appearance of 2 Ju87 Staffeln over Hawkinge and 2 more over Lympne with a massive force of  Me 109s providing cover.

Luckily for the airfields, 2 squadrons had been scrambled to patrol near Dover and were now in a position to intervene.

entries.name: IDS_QUICK_33_DESC
entries.text:
88 Dornier Do 17s escorted by over 120 Bf 109s crossed the coast at Deal.

The sector controller was only able to divert 3 airborne squadrons to meet this threat initially.

Near Faversham 1 Gruppe of bombers split off and turned NW towards Eastchurch while the rest continued on towards Rochester.

The Luftwaffe fighter screen proved very effective and few RAF fighters were able to make an impression on the bombers.
